issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps but code reads max_step
issues.detail: The docstring documents max_steps, val_interval, and deepspeed_config but the code reads trainer_args['max_step']. A typo on a required dict key is a runtime KeyError on first launch. Pick one name, fix the other, and add a real validation step that asserts required keys at __init__ time instead of crashing mid-setup.

issues.description: Checkpoint sort treats step_N as latest by name, picks wrong dir after partial save
issues.detail: load_checkpoint scans output_dir/checkpoints for any directory containing 'step_' and picks the highest number. If save_checkpoint crashed mid-write, you resume from a corrupt directory with no atomicity guard. Either write a 'latest' marker file on successful save, or verify the candidate is complete before loading. Silently resuming from junk is worse than not resuming.

issues.description: valid_*_specifier is split by whitespace, but the format embeds colon-delimited paths that can contain spaces
issues.detail: args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() silently splits on whitespace, but the documented format is 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' where data_json is a path. One space in a path and you get two bogus specs. train.py uses a single specifier without split. Pick one convention (comma-separated, or repeated --flag) and document it.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats mutates the caller's dict in place but train()/valid() also reassign stats; confusing ownership
issues.detail: _all_reduce_stats divides tensors in place, then the caller immediately rebuilds stats as a float dict. The in-place division means if the caller ever reuses the original tensor (e.g. for backward bookkeeping) the value is now world-size-divided. The contract should be either pure (return new dict) or clearly destructive. Right now it's both, which is how subtle bugs get written six months from now.

issues.description: run() loop never saves at max_step boundary correctly and double-validates on resume
issues.detail: The outer while loop calls train() (which advances global_step by save_interval), then valid(), then save. If global_step already equals max_step on resume, the loop exits without saving final state. If save_interval doesn't divide max_step, the last partial window also validates and checkpoints at an odd step. Make the loop boundary explicit and validate/save semantics deterministic.

issues.description: Non-rank-0 ranks set log_level='CRITICAL'; debugging a hang on rank 3 is now impossible
issues.detail: Silencing every rank but 0 below CRITICAL is convenient until a single GPU deadlocks or OOMs and you have nothing in the logs. At minimum keep ERROR/WARNING on all ranks, or gate this behind a --quiet-non-master flag. Rank-0-only INFO is fine; rank-N-silent is hostile to the person debugging at 2am.

review.summary: Patch lands a DeepSpeed trainer and a launcher in two files; structurally it's the right shape (one trainer, one entrypoint, clean separation). But it ships with a docstring/code key mismatch (max_steps vs max_step) that will KeyError on first run, a checkpoint-resume scan that has no atomicity guard against half-written directories, and a whitespace-split parser for path-bearing specifiers. The in-place mutation in _all_reduce_stats is the kind of "works today, breaks the next maintainer" taste smell. NEEDS-WORK: fix the key, harden checkpoint discovery, pick a real specifier delimiter, and stop muting non-zero ranks below CRITICAL.
